angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 466,815 km at 152.08 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.5756 +/- 0.0087 mas (same row, RUWE 1.03): 152.08 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.671 +/- 0.035 solar radii from Rowe et al. 2014, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-378 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJ...784...45R/abstract): 466,815 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.753 +/- 0.106428 solar masses from TICv8, the stellar mass of Kepler-378 b's parameter set from TICv8 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4661 +/- 100 K from Rowe et al. 2014, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-378 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJ...784...45R/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Rowe et al. 2014, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-378 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014ApJ...784...45R/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-378.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.661, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
